title: Last-Digit Detective
authorship: Original Primer explanations, examples and implementation. No Brilliant lesson text, artwork or question bank is included.

knowledge.definition: A positive integer d divides N when N = d × q for an integer q, leaving remainder zero.
knowledge.one_digit: Write N = 10 × q + r. When d divides 10, the tens contribute no remainder, so only r matters. This covers 2, 5 and 10.
knowledge.two_digits: Write N = 100 × q + r. Since 100 is a multiple of 4, divisibility by 4 depends on the final two digits.
knowledge.uncertainty: A final 0 alone does not settle divisibility by 4: 40 is divisible by 4, but 50 is not.
